title: Return Value
definition: A return value is the explicit result communicated by a function to its caller when normal control returns.
purpose: Let callers capture, test, compose, transform, or display a result independently from the function's internal work.
history: Function results support expression evaluation and composition; procedures may instead emphasize effects, but language terminology varies.
mental_model: Return is an output channel back to the waiting call site; printing sends information to a different observer and is not the same channel.
analogy: A service receipt handed back to the requester; it fails for exceptions, streaming, multiple asynchronous events, or mutation-only operations.
industry_notes: Explicit results make data flow inspectable; failure and effect channels must still be documented separately.
ai_notes: Ask AI to trace each return path and distinguish returned data from logs, mutation, and exceptions.
interview_notes: Ask how a returned value enables composition and why a printed value cannot be captured by the caller.
